thread:
customer_acme_eng: Hey team, hitting a bunch of 500s from our prod app since ~09:12 UTC, can you help? No obvious request id in our logs.

maddie (Support): Sorry about that — we can take a look. Can you paste one example request/response or the request timestamp and region? Also helpful: any request header that looks like `x-rw-request` or `x-correlator`.

customer_acme_eng: Timestamp was 2026-03-16T09:12:03Z, region eu-west-1. Response body just says `Internal Server Error`. We do have SDK logs (mobile) but not sure where the Redwood ID is.

maddie (Support): OK — we need the internal trace token so SRE can join spans. Quick checklist: 1) In the Console: Requests -> Search by time window -> click the failing request -> copy the header `x-redwood-correlator` (or `x-rw-request-id`). 2) From SDK logs: look for `request_id` or `correlator` in the log lines (Android logcat, iOS os_log). 3) If you can run a minimal curl repro, include the curl + response headers.

raj (SRE): If the Console route isn't available, you can also grab the request from the browser Network tab: select the POST to `/v1/generate` -> Headers -> Request Headers -> look for `x-rw-request-id` or `x-redwood-trace`. For mobile, the SDK emits `X-Redwood-Session` when debug mode is enabled.

customer_acme_eng: We only have mobile crash logs. Sample Android log line: `I/RedwoodClient: call failed, err=500, body='Internal Server Error'` — nothing else. How can I enable richer logs in prod briefly?

maddie (Support): You can enable short-lived SDK debug mode for a specific user/session: set env var `REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1` for the process or call `client.enableDebug(true)` in a non-blocking window. That will make the SDK emit a `redwood_correlator` header on each request and log `request_id: <hex>` to stdout. If that's not possible, we can ask for a HAR or a tcpdump from the device to extract headers.

customer_acme_eng: Can you show a minimal curl that includes the correlator head so we can reproduce?

maddie (Support): Sure — here's a minimal example. Replace <KEY> and <PAYLOAD>.

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Request-Source: mobile" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.1","input":"hello"}'
```

To attach a correlator manually when you can't change the client headers, add `-H "X-Redwood-Correlator: <your-id>"` and include the same header in the client's SDK logs if available.

raj (SRE): If you can include response headers in the curl output, that helps. `-i` prints them. Look specifically for `x-redwood-trace` or `x-redwood-request-id`. If present, paste the full header string here. Also include the exact UTC timestamp (to the second) and region — that narrows the trace.

customer_acme_eng: Ran the curl above from our CI at 09:12:03Z, got this header back: `x-redwood-request-id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-1234-abcdef567890`. Also saw `x-server-region: eu-west-1`.

maddie (Support): Perfect, thanks. Can you also upload the mobile SDK debug log (pastebin or attached text). If you have a HAR or network capture, include that too. If you can't share raw logs, at minimum give us: the request id (you already did), client version, SDK config (timeout, retries), and a short repro curl.

raj (SRE): We'll run a trace join with that request id. One more ask: if the request touched an authorization layer, include the `Authorization` header's prefix (e.g., `Bearer`) and the subscription id (no secret tokens). This helps us check quota/billing triggers without seeing tokens.

customer_acme_eng: Got it — attaching logs now. Anything else we should send for a faster turnaround?

maddie (Support): If possible, also include: 1) a short HAR export from the browser or a tcpdump (pcap) from the device for the same timeframe, 2) the region and the exact endpoint used, 3) whether this affected one user or many. Add `#escalate` reaction and we'll loop in infra if trace shows backend 502/503 cascades. :thumbsup:

customer_acme_eng: Uploaded logs and HAR to the case. Thanks, will wait for your update.

raj (SRE): Received — starting trace correlation. If we need to flip any internal flags to increase logging for that timeframe we'll let you know, but request id you provided is a good start.

maddie (Support): Thanks — I'll keep this thread updated, moving to high priority.
